source_direct_findings: The official Qwen3-ASR-0.6B configuration lists German as a supported language.
The official 0.6B model artifact is safetensors and the observed weight pointer reports 1,876,091,704 bytes with SHA-256 79d6cbd4c98c7bbffe9db2edac07f56cd6637d0d5944b27f6c2b8353840323ea.
The official streaming demo is explicitly a vLLM-backend path and installs through qwen-asr[vllm].
The official streaming documentation states that streaming inference does not support batch inference or returning timestamps.
Offline/non-streaming inference can use a forced aligner for timestamps; that does not establish streaming timestamp capability.
project_inferences_not_runtime_facts: A vLLM-only official streaming path may impose meaningful resident-memory/runtime coexistence cost when ASR shares the LOCAL-SOLO host with Frankenstein's LLM, TTS, GRID/GWT/J-Space, UnifiedDB and background services; this must be measured on clay-direct-dev.
Frankenstein turn-taking, cancellation and causal speech-state bookkeeping must not assume streaming ASR word timestamps unless a separate measured timestamp path is admitted.
The 0.6B artifact is source-admissible as a German-capable streaming candidate, but it has no Frankenstein German WER, partial-stability, TTFT/endpoint-latency or long-session credit yet.
counterhypothesis_note: The inspected official source does not document an equivalent non-vLLM streaming backend or streaming timestamp return path. This is a source observation, not proof that no alternative implementation exists outside the official runtime.
